description: close_call / close_call run where the two options overlap and one connection reverses the ordering. This is the fixture that exercises the served TONE table at caution rank 1 ("clear lead", "obvious" forbidden) and the R-CONT fabricated-callback guard.

provenance.note: Revived; edge ids added, flip_threshold_data added, and the readiness/headline_type pair kept so the tone row resolves to the close_call row rather than being asserted by hand. | FLIP_THRESHOLDS GOLDEN CORRECTED 2026-07-31 (fix-decision-review-v15 lane, disclosed): the golden flip_thresholds entries were hand-written as { factor_label, current, flip_at, note } with rounded values. Two independent defects. (a) FIELD NAMES: the runtime contract is { factor_id, factor_label, current_display, flip_display, narrative } (src/orchestrator-v5/compose/phase3-blocks.ts:1703-1765 reads factor_id/factor_label/narrative and DROPS any entry missing one), so the old goldens described a shape production would discard entirely — a golden nothing could ever produce. (b) VALUE FORM: the served v14 prompt contradicts itself here — :344-350 orders the raw value verbatim while :116-118/:220 order the percentage form and no_raw_probability_decimals scores the raw form as a failure. The goldens now follow the NON-self-contradictory rule (percentage form) and the runtime field names. The prompt-side resolution is drafted but NOT YET PROMOTED (tools/orchestrator-eval/drafts/decision_review.v15-draft.txt); until it is, this fixture encodes the contract the runtime and the scorer agree on, not the flip bullet the served prompt still carries.

input.brief: Do we move the team to a four day week or keep the current schedule?

candidates.label: good
candidates.note: Hedged in the way the close_call tone row requires. Should PASS.

output.narrative_summary: Move to Four Day Week is ahead by about 6 percentage points over Keep Current Schedule, which is inside the range the model cannot separate. Delivery throughput is the fragility that decides it.

story_headlines.opt_four_day: Slightly ahead, but only while delivery throughput holds
story_headlines.opt_status_quo: Close behind and less exposed to throughput loss

robustness_explanation.summary: The ordering holds in only about 56% of runs, so the two options are hard to separate.
robustness_explanation.primary_risk: Delivery throughput could fall far enough to reverse the ordering.
fragility_factors: Delivery throughput reverses the ordering in about 41% of runs.

output.readiness_rationale: The two options sit close together, so more can be learned about delivery throughput before committing.

fac_throughput.why: Delivery throughput is both the least well supported input and the one that separates the options.
fac_throughput.expected_gain: Would separate two options that currently overlap.

edge_throughput_margin.context: If delivery throughput drops, operating margin follows and Keep Current Schedule moves ahead.

flip_thresholds.narrative: If Delivery Throughput moves from 44% to 49%, the leading option changes. A small move reverses the ordering.

key_assumptions: Delivery throughput responds to the schedule change within the period modelled.
Staff retention gains hold beyond the first year.
